questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes with steady deceleration of 4 m/s^2. How long until it stops?

options.text: 10 s, using stopping distance divided by initial speed
options.misconception: confuses stopping time with stopping distance

options.text: 4 s, treating deceleration value as elapsed time
5 s, from v = u + at with final speed zero
20 s, keeping initial speed as the time value
options.misconception: equates speed value with time value

questions.explanation: With steady deceleration, final speed zero gives t = u/a = 20/4 = 5 s; the other choices misapply the kinematic relation.
questions.hint: Set final velocity to zero and solve for time.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph the curve is flat at 6 m/s for 4 s then drops to zero. What is the velocity at 2 s?

options.text: 0 m/s, reading the final value at the end
options.misconception: reads the wrong point on the graph

options.text: 3 m/s, averaging start and end values
options.misconception: averages instead of reading the flat value

options.text: 6 m/s, the height of the flat segment
2 m/s, using time divided by velocity

questions.explanation: A flat segment means constant velocity, so at 2 s the value is 6 m/s; averaging or inverting gives wrong readings.
questions.hint: A horizontal line means constant velocity.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A velocity-time graph is a rectangle 5 m/s high and 8 s wide. Find the displacement.
questions.explanation: Displacement equals the area under the velocity-time graph, 5 times 8 = 40 m.
questions.hint: Multiply height by width for the rectangle area.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: A student integrates a(t)=2 m/s^2 twice and gets x(t)=t^2 + 5, dropping the initial velocity term. What is wrong?

options.text: The constant 5 should be the initial position only
options.misconception: ignores that integration constants carry initial conditions

options.text: The first integration must include v0, giving v(t)=2t+v0
Acceleration cannot be integrated twice in kinematics
The units of t^2 are seconds, not meters
options.misconception: confuses unit of time with unit of length

questions.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives velocity plus v0; dropping v0 removes the initial velocity contribution, so the position law is wrong.
questions.hint: First integration yields velocity with constant v0.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: A stone is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m. Using g=10 m/s^2, find the fall time.
questions.explanation: From h = (1/2) g t^2, t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(40/10) = 2 s.
questions.hint: Use h = half g t squared.

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: A runner completes a 400 m lap in 50 s. Find the average speed.
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance over total time, 400/50 = 8 m/s.
questions.hint: Divide total distance by total time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: Position is x(t)=3t^2+2t in meters. Find the velocity at t=4 s.
questions.explanation: Velocity is dx/dt = 6t+2, so at t=4 s it is 24+2 = 26 m/s.
questions.hint: Differentiate x(t) with respect to time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: Velocity is v(t)=5t-3 in m/s. Find the acceleration.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is dv/dt = 5 m/s^2, constant for all time.
questions.hint: Differentiate v(t) with respect to time.

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A bike at 12 m/s stops with steady deceleration of 3 m/s^2. What is the stopping time?

options.misconception: confuses stopping time with stopping distance

options.text: 4 s, from v = u + at with final speed zero
12 s, keeping initial speed as time
options.misconception: equates speed value with time value

questions.explanation: Final speed zero gives t = 12/3 = 4 s; the other options misapply the kinematic relation.
questions.hint: Set final velocity to zero and solve for time.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph the line rises linearly from 0 to 8 m/s over 4 s. What is the velocity at 2 s?

options.misconception: reads the wrong point on the graph
reads the wrong point on the graph

options.text: 4 m/s, halfway along the linear rise
2 m/s, using time divided by slope

questions.explanation: Linear rise from 0 to 8 over 4 s gives 2 m/s per second, so at 2 s velocity is 4 m/s.
questions.hint: Interpolate linearly along the segment.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: Which quantity equals the area under a velocity-time graph?

options.text: Acceleration, from the slope of the curve
Speed, from the height of the curve
Time, from the width of the curve

questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement; slope gives acceleration and height gives velocity.
questions.hint: Area under v-t graph represents displacement.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: Acceleration is a(t)=4 m/s^2 and initial velocity is 2 m/s. Find velocity at t=3 s.
questions.hint: Add initial velocity to a times t.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: A student computes fall time for 45 m using g=10 as t = 45/10 = 4.5 s. What is the error?

options.text: The formula should be t = sqrt(2h/g), not h/g

options.misconception: quibbles about g value instead of method

options.text: Height should be doubled before dividing
options.misconception: partial fix missing the square root

options.text: Time has no units in free fall

questions.explanation: Free fall distance is (1/2)gt^2, so t = sqrt(2h/g); dividing h by g ignores the square and the factor 2.
questions.hint: Solve h = half g t squared for t.

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: A cyclist rides 10 km out and 10 km back in 2 h total. What is the average speed?

options.text: 10 km/h, total distance over total time
20 km/h, adding the two legs' speeds
options.misconception: adds speeds instead of averaging over time

questions.explanation: Average speed uses total distance 20 km over 2 h = 10 km/h; zero displacement would be average velocity, not speed.
questions.hint: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: For x(t)=t^3, what is the velocity at t=2 s?
questions.explanation: Velocity is dx/dt = 3t^2, so at t=2 s it is 3*4 = 12 m/s.
questions.hint: Differentiate x(t) with respect to time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: Velocity is v(t)=2t^2+3t in m/s. Find the acceleration at t=1 s.
questions.explanation: a(t)=dv/dt=4t+3, so at t=1 s acceleration is 4+3 = 7 m/s^2.
questions.hint: Differentiate v(t) with respect to time.

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A truck at 30 m/s brakes steadily at 5 m/s^2. Find the stopping time.
questions.explanation: t = u/a = 30/5 = 6 s until velocity reaches zero.
questions.hint: Set final velocity to zero and solve for time.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A student says the velocity at 3 s on a v-t graph equals the slope at that point. What is wrong?

options.text: Velocity is the height, not the slope, of the v-t graph
The slope gives displacement, not velocity
Velocity cannot be read from a v-t graph
The value at 3 s is always zero

questions.explanation: On a velocity-time graph the vertical height gives velocity; the slope gives acceleration.
questions.hint: Height of v-t graph is velocity; slope is acceleration.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph is a triangle with base 6 s and height 9 m/s. Find the displacement.
questions.explanation: Area of triangle = (1/2)*base*height = 0.5*6*9 = 27 m.
questions.hint: Use half base times height.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: If acceleration is constant a, which expression gives position with initial velocity v0 and position x0?

options.misconception: omits the time factor on velocity

questions.explanation: Integrating constant acceleration twice yields x(t)=x0+v0 t+(1/2) a t^2.
questions.hint: Integrate acceleration twice with constants.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: Two stones are dropped from different heights. Which falls for the longer time?

options.text: The one dropped from the greater height
The one dropped from the lesser height
Both take the same time regardless of height

questions.explanation: Fall time grows with height via t = sqrt(2h/g), so the greater height gives longer time; mass does not matter.
questions.hint: Time increases with the square root of height.

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: A table shows distances 0, 50, 100, 150 m at times 0, 10, 20, 30 s. What is the average speed over 30 s?

options.text: 5 m/s, total distance over total time

questions.explanation: Total distance 150 m over 30 s gives 5 m/s; using one interval gives the same value here but for the wrong reason.
questions.hint: Divide total distance by total time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: A student differentiates x(t)=4t^2+1 and writes v(t)=8t, forgetting the derivative of the constant. Is the velocity correct?

options.text: Yes, the derivative of 1 is 0, so v(t)=8t is correct
No, the derivative of 1 is 1, giving 8t+1

questions.explanation: The derivative of a constant is zero, so v(t)=8t is correct; the other options misuse differentiation rules.
questions.hint: Derivative of a constant is zero.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: If v(t) is linear in t, what is the acceleration?

options.misconception: confuses changing velocity with zero acceleration

questions.explanation: A linear velocity function has constant slope, hence constant acceleration.
questions.hint: Acceleration is the slope of v(t).

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A v-t graph shows velocity falling linearly from 15 to 0 m/s over 5 s. Find the deceleration.
questions.explanation: Deceleration is the slope (0-15)/5 = -3 m/s^2.
questions.hint: Compute slope of the v-t line.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph is flat at 7 m/s. What is the velocity at 10 s?
questions.explanation: A flat segment means constant velocity of 7 m/s at every instant.
questions.hint: Horizontal line means constant velocity.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A student finds displacement for a triangular v-t graph by multiplying base by height, ignoring the half. What is wrong?

options.text: Triangle area needs half the product of base and height
The graph should be a rectangle, not a triangle
Height should be squared before multiplying
Base and height are the same quantity

questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is half base times height; omitting the half doubles the displacement.
questions.hint: Triangle area is half base times height.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: Given x(t)=2t^2+3t+1, what is the initial position?
questions.explanation: At t=0, x(0)=1 m, so the constant term is the initial position.
questions.hint: Evaluate x at t=0.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: A ball is dropped from 45 m with g=10 m/s^2. Find the fall time.
questions.hint: Use t = sqrt(2h/g).

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: A car travels 60 km in 1.5 h. Find the average speed in km/h.
questions.explanation: Average speed = 60/1.5 = 40 km/h.
questions.hint: Divide distance by time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: For x(t)=5t+2, the velocity is?
questions.explanation: Velocity is dx/dt = 5 m/s, constant.
questions.hint: Differentiate the linear term.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: v(t)=3t^2. What is acceleration at t=2 s?
questions.explanation: a(t)=dv/dt=6t, so at t=2 s acceleration is 12 m/s^2.
questions.hint: Differentiate v(t).

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A student uses t = v/a with v=10, a=2 and gets 5 s, but the object was speeding up, not slowing down. What is wrong?

options.text: Deceleration sign makes stopping time undefined here
The formula gives time to reach zero only if a opposes motion
Speeding up means time is negative
You must use distance, not velocity

questions.explanation: t = v/a gives time to zero speed only when acceleration opposes velocity; otherwise speed never reaches zero.
questions.hint: Check that acceleration opposes motion.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: On a v-t graph, a negative value means?

options.text: The object moves in the opposite direction

questions.explanation: Negative velocity indicates motion opposite to the chosen positive direction.
questions.hint: Sign of velocity indicates direction.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph is flat at -4 m/s for 5 s. Find the displacement.
questions.explanation: Area = (-4)*5 = -20 m, negative because motion is opposite direction.
questions.hint: Multiply velocity by time, keeping sign.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: a(t)=6 m/s^2, v0=0, x0=0. Find position at t=2 s.
questions.hint: Use half a t squared.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: A table lists heights 5, 20, 45 m with fall times 1, 2, 3 s (g=10). Which height gives 2 s?
questions.explanation: For g=10, t=sqrt(2h/10); t=2 s gives h=20 m.
questions.hint: Match time to height using t squared.

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: A student computes average speed for a round trip as (v1+v2)/2. When is this wrong?

options.text: Always, unless the times for each leg are equal
Never, averaging speeds is always valid

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean of speeds is correct only when the two legs take equal time; otherwise use total distance over total time.
questions.hint: Average speed weights by time, not by leg.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: x(t)=t^2-4t+7. Find velocity at t=3 s.
questions.explanation: v(t)=2t-4, so at t=3 s velocity is 6-4 = 2 m/s.
questions.hint: Differentiate x(t).

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: v(t)=4t^3. Find acceleration at t=1 s.
questions.explanation: a(t)=12t^2, so at t=1 s acceleration is 12 m/s^2.
questions.hint: Differentiate v(t).

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A car at 25 m/s stops in 5 s. Find the deceleration.

options.text: -5 m/s^2, from change in velocity over time

questions.hint: Divide change in velocity by time.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph has a jump from 2 to 6 m/s at t=3 s. What is velocity just after 3 s?

options.text: 2 m/s, the value before the jump
6 m/s, the value after the jump

questions.explanation: Just after the jump the graph height is 6 m/s.
questions.hint: Read the height just after the discontinuity.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: For motion with negative velocity, the area under the v-t graph is?
questions.explanation: Signed area under v-t graph gives signed displacement; negative velocity yields negative displacement.
questions.hint: Area carries the sign of velocity.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: A student integrates a(t)=2t and writes v(t)=t^2, omitting the constant. Is the velocity correct?

options.text: Yes if initial velocity is zero

questions.explanation: Integral of 2t is t^2 + C; if v0=0 then C=0 and v(t)=t^2 is correct.
questions.hint: The constant equals initial velocity.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: If height quadruples, fall time?

options.text: Doubles, since time scales with sqrt(height)

questions.explanation: t = sqrt(2h/g), so quadrupling h doubles t.
questions.hint: Time scales with square root of height.

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: A runner does 2 laps of 400 m in 100 s. Find average speed.
questions.explanation: Total distance 800 m over 100 s = 8 m/s.
questions.hint: Divide total distance by total time.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: x(t)=6t^2. What is velocity at t=0?
questions.explanation: v(t)=12t, so at t=0 velocity is 0 m/s.
questions.hint: Differentiate then evaluate at 0.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: A student says acceleration is zero whenever velocity is zero. What is wrong?

options.text: Acceleration can be nonzero at an instant when velocity is zero
Acceleration is always zero at t=0

questions.explanation: At the top of a throw velocity is zero but acceleration is g downward, nonzero.
questions.hint: Acceleration is independent of instantaneous velocity.

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A sprinter at 8 m/s decelerates steadily at 2 m/s^2. Find stopping time.
questions.hint: Divide speed by deceleration.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph slopes downward. The object is?
questions.explanation: A downward slope with positive velocity means deceleration; the object may still move forward.
questions.hint: Slope sign relative to velocity sign determines acceleration.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph is a rectangle 3 m/s by 10 s followed by a triangle base 4 s height 3 m/s. Total displacement?
questions.explanation: Rectangle 3*10=30 plus triangle 0.5*4*3=6 gives 36 m.
questions.hint: Sum rectangle and triangle areas.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: a(t)=2, v0=3, x0=1. Find x at t=2.
questions.hint: Use x0 + v0 t + half a t squared.

questions.topic: Time of a fall under gravity
questions.learningObjective: Compute fall time under gravity
questions.stem: A student says a heavy stone falls faster than a light one. What is wrong?

options.text: In vacuum all objects fall with same acceleration g
Heavy objects have more inertia, so slower

questions.explanation: Without air resistance, all objects fall with acceleration g independent of mass.
questions.hint: Free fall acceleration is independent of mass.

questions.topic: Average speed on a closed circuit
questions.learningObjective: Compute average speed on a closed circuit
questions.stem: On a closed circuit the average velocity is?
questions.explanation: Average velocity is displacement over time, and displacement is zero on a closed circuit.
questions.hint: Velocity uses displacement, not distance.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate position to get velocity
questions.stem: x(t)=7 (constant). Find velocity.
questions.explanation: Derivative of a constant is 0, so velocity is 0 m/s.
questions.hint: Derivative of constant is zero.

questions.learningObjective: Differentiate velocity to get acceleration
questions.stem: If v(t) is quadratic in t, acceleration is?
questions.explanation: Derivative of a quadratic is linear.
questions.hint: Differentiate reduces degree by one.

questions.learningObjective: Compute stopping time from steady deceleration
questions.stem: A graph shows speed vs time dropping from 10 to 0 over 2 s. Stopping time is?
questions.explanation: The time to reach zero speed is the horizontal width, 2 s.
questions.hint: Read the time axis at zero speed.

questions.learningObjective: Read velocity from a velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A v-t graph reads 9 m/s at t=4 s. What is velocity?
questions.explanation: The height of the v-t graph at that point is the velocity, 9 m/s.
questions.hint: Read the vertical value.

questions.topic: Displacement as the area under a graph
questions.learningObjective: Compute displacement as area under velocity-time graph
questions.stem: A student computes displacement by integrating acceleration instead of velocity. What is wrong?

options.text: Displacement comes from integrating velocity, not acceleration

questions.explanation: Displacement is the integral of velocity; integrating acceleration gives velocity.
questions.hint: Match the integrand to the desired quantity.

questions.learningObjective: Integrate acceleration to find position
questions.stem: To find position from a(t), how many integrations are needed?
questions.explanation: Integrate acceleration to get velocity, then integrate velocity to get position: two integrations.
questions.hint: Acceleration to velocity to position.
